subject: Action Required: Major customer - Token verification failures triggering retry flood
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@logicloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@logicloud.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: 5xx/429 + timeouts impacting production - urgent

Hi Vanessa / Redwood team,

We started seeing a dramatic uptick in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood endpoint for our ingestion flow around 07:15 PT this morning. Throughput dropped by ~60% and our downstream queues are filling. Can you confirm whether this is on your side? We see logs referencing token validation failures and the requests look valid on our end.

This is affecting customers in APAC and EU as well. Please escalate — we need a mitigation plan within 2 hours.

Regards,
Aisha
Head of SRE, LogiCloud
[attachment: log-snippet-20270801.txt (text/plain)]

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@logicloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429 + timeouts impacting production - urgent

Aisha — thank you for the heads-up and the log excerpt, that was very helpful. I’m spinning up an incident bridge and looping in runtime/infra. Initial ask: can you confirm whether your token issuer rotated keys or changed time skew settings in the last 24 hours? The logs you attached show repeated 5xx and 429 at the gateway while the backend returned auth failure traces.

On our side we’re seeing a cascading retry pattern from clients (including yours) that amplifies the load and makes auth failures look like gateway 5xx/429. We’ll prioritize a triage to separate genuine server errors from misclassified auth failures.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Working hypothesis: token validation failures due to clock drift (JWT exp/nbf checks) that our gateway currently surfaces as 5xx/429 during a retry flood.
- Marcus + Monica will confirm gateway logs and adjust short-term rate limiting/fail-open behavior.
- Rishi to prepare a classification patch so auth rejects are surfaced as 401/403 instead of 5xx/429 where appropriate.

Bridge: https://redwood.inc/bridge/INC-20270801-van
Vanessa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429 + timeouts impacting production - urgent

On the bridge now. Quick notes from infra:
- At 07:12 PT we started seeing 429 spikes across a set of customer routes (including LogiCloud).
- Gateway logs show an increase in token validation failures: signature checks pass but exp/nbf claims failing due to clock skew of ~5-7 minutes from the issuer (LogiCloud) compared to Redwood’s clock.
- Our current behavior: gateway returns 5xx/429 in some timeout/queue-overflow paths during high retry pressure (this is ambiguous and causing incorrect alerting).

Immediate mitigations we applied (09:00):
1) Scoped rate-limit backoff for LogiCloud routes to reduce retry amplification.
2) Short-term increase of accepted JWT skew window from 2 minutes to 10 minutes (config flip) for routes that have been triaged.
3) Routing fallback to warm model-pool nodes to reduce queue timeouts.

We need follow-ups: a permanent fix to classification and a postmortem with LogiCloud.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Tamir

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@logicloud.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429 + timeouts impacting production - urgent

Post-triage update:
- Confirmed root cause: clock skew from LogiCloud token issuer (~+6 minutes) led to a high rate of nbf/exp failures. Under typical traffic this would surface as 401, but under the retry storm and queue pressure some validation timeouts bubbled up as 429/5xx.
- Actions completed: 1) Scoped JWT skew window increase applied to LogiCloud ingestion routes. 2) Classification fix staged: gateway will map token validation failures explicitly to 401/403 and will not convert to 5xx even during queue overload. 3) Temporary client-side guidance sent to LogiCloud: backoff/retry jitter and reduce aggressive exponential retry.

We will revert the skew window to default once LogiCloud stabilizes and issues a config patch to restore clock sync. Permanent fix (priority): ensure gateway validation path is non-blocking and always returns auth-specific status codes.

Action items assigned:
- Rishi: deploy classification patch to canary (INF-4821). ETA: EOD Aug 2.
- Marcus: run capacity soak and update autoscaling thresholds to resist retry storms. ETA: Aug 3.
- Vanessa: coordinate exec brief / credits conversation with LogiCloud leadership.

Monica
VP, Production Reliability

---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@logicloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429 + timeouts impacting production - urgent

Aisha — following our remediation and LogiCloud’s clock fix, your ingestion pipeline has stabilized. Thank you for rapid coordination.

Executive summary for your leadership:
- Incident: elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts (07:12–09:45 PT 2027-08-01) caused by JWT time validation failures amplified by client retry patterns.
- Impact: 60% throughput reduction for LogiCloud routes; ~45 minutes of degraded service before mitigations.
- Root cause: ~6 minute clock drift at token issuer combined with gateway behavior that could surface auth failures as 5xx/429 under load.
- Immediate mitigations: scoped JWT skew window expansion, targeted rate-limit backoff, routing fallbacks.
- Permanent work: classification patch to ensure auth failures return 401/403 and do not degrade system queues; improved observability to detect auth vs server errors; guidance for client-side retry jitter.

We’re prepared to provide a formal postmortem and timeline. Vanessa will reach out to schedule a leadership call to discuss credits and SLA remediation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
